text.p: Thousands of Australian public servants walked off the job on Tuesday as part of an ongoing industrial dispute with the government over employment conditions.

"The widespread rejection of the budget has shown that the government has no real answers to the problems facing Australia," Community and Public Sector Union national secretary Wendy Caird said in a statement.
"It seems the only thing they know how to do is slash public service jobs, sell off multinational conglomerates and close government offices."
Caird said half day stoppages began at 2.00 p.m. (0400 GMT) in the state of New South Wales and would continue on a state-by-state basis over the next fortnight.

Public servants in South Australia and the Northern Territory would stop work on May 22, followed by the Australian Capital Territory on May 26, Victoria on May 27 and Western Australia, Queensland and Tasmania on May 29.
